contradictions.fact: which approach this route describes — Esmeralda Basin/Fortune Creek Pass vs. De Roux Creek Trail

claims.says: The line described here climbs out of Esmeralda Basin toward Fortune Creek Pass ... the peaks can also be reached from the east via the De Roux Creek Trail, a separate, steeper scree scramble
From the De Roux trailhead (3,800 ft), follow the Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392 roughly 3 miles west ... to a scree field near the final switchback (~5,600 ft)
Start at the Esmeralda Basin / Ingalls Lake Trailhead ... Esmeralda Basin Trail #1394 ... tops out at Fortune Creek Pass
descend the same Class 2 talus/scree slope back down to Fortune Creek Pass ... rejoin the maintained Esmeralda Basin Trail #1394 ... retracing the ~3.5 mi hike-in
De Roux trailhead (3,800 ft) on Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392 ... up the valley between Esmeralda Peaks and Koppen Mountain ... to a scree field near ~5,600 ft
'Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392 to the last switchback' — 'This is the standard approach.'
Leave the maintained trail at or just below Fortune Creek Pass and angle east/northeast...

contradictions.why: Two real, mutually exclusive approaches to the same summit (west-side Esmeralda Basin/Fortune Creek Pass Trail #1394, vs. east-side De Roux Creek/Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392) are named as THIS route's approach in different fields: overview, approach (prose), descent_text and climbing_route all describe Fortune Creek Pass, while beta, pitch_detail and approach_variants (which explicitly calls it 'the standard approach') describe De Roux. A climber cross-checking Overview against Plan would be sent to two different trailheads on opposite sides of the mountain.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Slightly more fields (overview, approach, descent_text, climbing_route) describe the Fortune Creek Pass line, and the itinerary's schedule/trailhead elevation (4,269 ft) matches that approach; beta/pitch_detail/approach_variants describing De Roux appear to be contaminated from the sibling route mentioned in overview.
